chapter_title: Automated Checks, Cost, and Student Privacy
learning_objective: The learner will classify each of eight problems by the automated check that finds it, or as one that no scan finds, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** automated-check-matcher
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify each of eight problems by the automated check that finds it, or as one that no scan finds, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Automated Link Checker, Automated Accessibility Scan, Automated License Detection, Automated Readability Scan (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each problem the learner commits one of five options. A choice is correct when it matches the Correct option column in Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the table of what each scan finds is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A clean accessibility scan means the page is accessible. (2) A license tool can tell whether a license claim is true. (3) A link checker can tell whether the cited content is right. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying a problem by the check that finds it is an Understand-level action that teaches the limits of each scan. Two problems that no scan finds teach the learner that automation leaves gaps. **Content:** The five options: Link checker, Accessibility scan, License detection, Readability scan, No scan finds it. The eight problems: | # | Problem shown to the learner | Correct option | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | A link in the reference list returns "page not found". | Link checker | A link checker tests exactly this. | | 2 | An image has no alt attribute at all. | Accessibility scan | A scan detects a missing alt attribute. | | 3 | The footer says CC BY-NC, and the metadata says CC BY. | License detection | License detection compares the two statements. | | 4 | A passage measures at grade 11 for a grade 6 audience. | Readability scan | A readability scan computes the grade level. | | 5 | The alt text says only "photo". | No scan finds it | A scan sees that alt text exists and cannot judge whether it is useful. | | 6 | White text on a pale yellow background has a contrast ratio of 1.4 to 1. | Accessibility scan | A scan computes contrast ratios. | | 7 | A statistic in the text is ten years out of date. | No scan finds it | Only a person with a current source can tell. | | 8 | No license statement appears anywhere in the resource. | License detection | License detection reports that no license was found. | **Provenance:** The problems are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The matches follow the chapter section "Automated Checks". **Rules:** Each problem has exactly one correct option. One is Link checker, two are Accessibility scan, two are License detection, one is Readability scan, and two are No scan finds it. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one problem and the five options. 2. The learner may open the table of what each scan finds. Opening it does not change the score. 3. The learner chooses an option, and the choice is committed. 4. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 5. After problem 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 problems in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [option]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The answer is [option]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You know what each scan can and cannot see." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed problem. **Starting State:** The first problem and the five options. The question shown is "Which automated check would find this?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's table lists what the link checker, accessibility scan, license detection, and readability scan each find and cannot find.
